feedIntervalMinutes.source: CDC: How Much and How Often to Feed Infant Formula; AAP/HealthyChildren: How Often to Breastfeed (docs/06)
feedIntervalMinutes.note: Day interval; night gap should not exceed ~4 h (S3).

feedDurationMinutes.source: DESIGN_ASSUMPTION: childcare reviewer decision 2026-11-19 (review sheet): "Since this is a simulation, the somewhat shorter feedings will suffice". Previously 10–25 (typical 15) (DESIGN_ASSUMPTION): no bottle-feed duration source; breastfeeding reference 10 + up to 15 min. Context: AAP/HealthyChildren symptom checker: Breastfeeding questions

feedsPer24h.source: DESIGN_ASSUMPTION: childcare reviewer decision 2026-11-19 (review sheet): "For this simulation, fewer feedings, specifically at night, will be sufficient". Previously 8–12 (typical 10) (GUIDANCE): CDC: How Much and How Often to Feed Infant Formula; AAP/HealthyChildren: How Often to Breastfeed; CDC: Newborn Breastfeeding Basics (docs/06)

feedAcceptMin.source: DESIGN_ASSUMPTION: childcare reviewer decision 2026-11-19 (review sheet): "For a doll simulation.  This is not relevant". Previously 0.5 (DESIGN_ASSUMPTION): no adequate source found; reviewer to decide (docs/06)

totalSleepHours24.source: DESIGN_ASSUMPTION: childcare reviewer decision 2026-11-19 (review sheet): "All sleep in a night, naps during the day for this simulation". Previously 14–17 (typical 15.5) (PEER_REVIEWED): Hirshkowitz et al. 2015, National Sleep Foundation sleep duration recommendations (docs/06)

napsPerDay.source: DESIGN_ASSUMPTION: childcare reviewer decision 2026-11-19 (review sheet): "A 2- to 3-hour nap every four hours per day, but this does not include nights and may be subject to change". Previously null (GUIDANCE): BC Children's Hospital: Healthy Sleep for Kids, Newborns (docs/06)
napsPerDay.note: No distinct naps: sleep is spread across day and night (circadian rhythm not yet present).

wakeWindowMinutes.source: DESIGN_ASSUMPTION: wake windows have no peer-reviewed basis; chosen to fit total sleep. Context: Romper: Are wake windows evidence based? (no evidence found)

sleepCycleMinutes.source: BC Children's Hospital: Healthy Sleep for Kids, Newborns (docs/06)
sleepCycleMinutes.note: Reviewer asked for 2-3 h day naps; owner approved doing that with dayNapMinutes and keeping the 50-60 min cycle.

dayNapMinutes.source: DESIGN_ASSUMPTION: childcare reviewer decision 2026-11-19 (review sheet), confirmed by owner: "2 to 3 hour naptimes throughout the day". Hunger or a dirty diaper still wakes the baby earlier.
dayNapMinutes.note: Daytime nap length: sleep cycles link until it is reached.

catnapProb.source: DESIGN_ASSUMPTION: Claude's reading of the reviewer note "a few exceptions of a random 20 minute nap sporadically"; reviewer to confirm
catnapProb.note: Chance a daytime nap is a short catnap (model.catnapMinutes) instead.

nightWakings.source: DESIGN_ASSUMPTION: childcare reviewer decision 2026-11-19 (review sheet): "This is for a simulation, not a real baby, so fewer night wakings are fine". Previously 2–4 (typical 3) (GUIDANCE): AAP/HealthyChildren: How Often to Breastfeed; Galland et al. 2012, Normal sleep patterns in infants and children (systematic review) (docs/06)
nightWakings.note: Derived from 8-12 feeds and <=4 h night gap (S3). S8 reports ~1.7 parent-reported for 0-2 m.

fussCryMinutesPer24h.source: DESIGN_ASSUMPTION: engine target below the published norm. Context: Wolke, Bilgin, Samara 2017, Fussing and crying durations meta-analysis (J Pediatr)
fussCryMinutesPer24h.note: Owner decision 2026-11-19: target the lower half of real-infant norms; revisit in M9 testing. Norm: 117-133 min mean (S11). Reviewer's "3" (2026-11-19) meant 3-minute fussy spells 16:00-24:00, applied as model.fussSpellMinutes and the evening window; this daily total is still unreviewed.

eveningFussClustering.source: Barr et al., normal crying curve and evening clustering (docs/06)

circadianStrength.source: DESIGN_ASSUMPTION: childcare reviewer decision 2026-11-19 (review sheet). Previously 0–0.1 (typical 0.05) (DESIGN_ASSUMPTION): newborns show no circadian rhythm; small nonzero allowance. Context: BC Children's Hospital: Healthy Sleep for Kids, Newborns

wetDiapersPerDay.source: DESIGN_ASSUMPTION: childcare reviewer decision 2026-11-19 (review sheet). Previously 6–10 (typical 8) (GUIDANCE): AAP/HealthyChildren: How to Tell if Your Breastfed Baby is Getting Enough Milk (docs/06)
wetDiapersPerDay.note: S13 gives >= 6/day by day 5-7; upper bound is a design choice.

soiledDiapersPerDay.source: DESIGN_ASSUMPTION: childcare reviewer decision 2026-11-19 (review sheet). Previously 3–5 (typical 4) (SECONDARY): Flo Health: How many diapers does a newborn use (docs/06)

vocalRepertoire.note: No coos yet: sounds other than crying are expected by ~2 months (S15).

vocalRatePerAwakeHour.source: DESIGN_ASSUMPTION: childcare reviewer decision 2026-11-19 (review sheet). Previously 2–6 (typical 4) (DESIGN_ASSUMPTION): no adequate source found; reviewer to decide (docs/06)

boredAfterMinutes.source: DESIGN_ASSUMPTION: boredom not modeled below ~4 months

careSustainMinutes.source: DESIGN_ASSUMPTION: no adequate source found; reviewer to decide (docs/06)

crySegmentMaxMinutes.source: DESIGN_ASSUMPTION: childcare reviewer decision 2026-11-19 (review sheet), confirmed by owner. The alert stays open after the crying stops until a caregiver responds (owner decision, docs/01). Previously 30.0 (DESIGN_ASSUMPTION): unattended crying cap before exhausted sleep (docs/01 B1)
crySegmentMaxMinutes.note: Longest crying spell before the baby falls asleep exhausted.

selfSettleProbNight.source: DESIGN_ASSUMPTION: no adequate source found; reviewer to decide (docs/06)
